1. **[high] Automatic titles contradict the privacy opt-in requirement.**  
   **Reference:** §Behavior rules: “Titles are auto-generated by the cheapest connected model”; §Rev 2: titles respect allowed providers.  
   **Why it matters:** An allowed provider is not consent to an additional background call. `12-security-and-privacy.md` explicitly makes title generation opt-in per project/folder, while chat also supports conversations without a project.  
   **Concrete fix:** Default to a local title derived from the first message. Define explicit AI-title consent for standalone conversations and project inheritance; select only an allowed, verified provider and skip generation when none qualifies.

2. **[high] Agent mentions conceal a separate data-transfer boundary.**  
   **Reference:** §Composer: “`@` to mention … an agent”; §Slash commands: “`/hermes <directive>`.”  
   **Why it matters:** `07` makes an agent mention an actual handoff, and `06` places Hermes on a VPS with persistent memory and optional Telegram echo. The provider disclosure in §Rev 2 does not explain which transcript, files, or project material reaches that remote agent.  
   **Concrete fix:** Specify a handoff preview identifying the agent, VPS destination, exact context, file-transfer method, and Telegram echo state. Apply gateway approval where required. Mention selection should prepare the handoff; explicit Send should execute it.

3. **[high] Retry and branch lack rules for previously executed actions.**  
   **Reference:** §Messages: “retry with another model, branch from this message.”  
   **Why it matters:** A response may already have created a task, written a file, or sent something before failing. Retrying the prompt could repeat those actions; branching could copy pending tool requests or approvals. `03` and `05` already restrict retries after side effects, but chat does not explain its behavior.  
   **Concrete fix:** Distinguish response regeneration from action retry. Preserve an immutable execution record, show completed actions before retry, invalidate inherited approvals, and never automatically re-execute completed actions. Define the branch point and copied context explicitly.

4. **[high] “Plain messages” leaves cross-model replay unsafe and unpredictable.**  
   **Reference:** §Behavior rules: “history is replayed as plain messages”; §Rev 2: warn about attachments/tool results.  
   **Why it matters:** The spec does not define whether replay includes thinking, tool arguments, tool results, partial answers, or attachment contents. Flattening these can lose the untrusted-data boundaries required by `12`. Different context limits also make “history” an unreliable promise.  
   **Concrete fix:** Define a canonical replay format preserving roles and provenance. Exclude private/internal reasoning and approval tokens; wrap tool/file content as untrusted data. Preview the actual outbound context, with explicit overflow handling rather than silent truncation.

5. **[med] The send API conflicts with the shared event-stream architecture.**  
   **Reference:** §API sketch: `POST /conversations/:id/messages … -> SSE of RunEvent`.  
   **Why it matters:** `01-architecture.md` specifies HTTP commands plus a shared, resumable SSE subscription. The sketch instead couples submission and streaming without defining acknowledgement, deduplication, or recovery when the connection drops after the daemon accepts a prompt.  
   **Concrete fix:** Have POST return durable message/run IDs and consume output through the shared sequenced stream. Add a client request ID for idempotent submission. Define recovery so reconnecting cannot create a second run or discard partial output.

6. **[med] Phase boundaries make the apparent chat scope substantially larger than the release plan.**  
   **Reference:** §Features and §Acceptance criteria; “Compare mode (phase 3).”  
   **Why it matters:** Most features have no phase assignment, although the roadmap puts scheduling in Phase 2, agents/Kanban in Phase 3, and indexing/search/compare in Phase 4. Compare explicitly contradicts that roadmap. Meanwhile, Phase 1 acceptance covers Claude only, whereas `13` requires Claude and Codex.  
   **Concrete fix:** Add a feature-to-phase table, align compare with Phase 4, distinguish basic attachments from indexed project search, and make both initial adapters part of Phase 1 acceptance. Keep unavailable future commands out of the active command menu.

7. **[med] Connection handling collapses states that need different actions.**  
   **Reference:** §Model picker: “disabled providers show a Connect link”; Phase 1 acceptance: logged-out provider blocks sending.  
   **Why it matters:** `03` distinguishes `needs_login`, `rate_limited`, `unavailable`, `degraded`, and `unknown`. Connect cannot resolve all of them, especially an unsupported adapter. Model changes also lack a rule for an effort value unsupported by the newly selected model.  
   **Concrete fix:** Define picker copy/actions for each shared connection state. Validate model/effort server-side; when switching invalidates effort, select a supported default and announce the change. Show the requested and actual fallback model separately.

8. **[med] The layout has no chat-specific width or collapse rules.**  
   **Reference:** §Layout: conversation list, thread, composer, collapsible Context panel.  
   **Why it matters:** `14` defines sheets below 900px, but chat does not say when to collapse its conversation list or Context panel above that breakpoint. Historical mockup dimensions could squeeze the thread, especially with tables, code, zoom, and a growing composer.  
   **Concrete fix:** Specify minimum thread width, panel collapse priority, and initial panel state. Preserve the shared 760px reading-width cap; allow code/tables to scroll within their own blocks. Define a bounded composer height and verify the layout at 900px, 200% zoom, and short viewport heights.

9. **[med] Message chrome has no hierarchy or density budget.**  
   **Reference:** §Messages lists model/effort/route, thinking, tool cards, retry, branch, Kanban, and save actions.  
   **Why it matters:** Giving every element equal prominence would make the thread read like a stack of control panels. Neither `04` nor the shared UI spec defines chat body sizing, message spacing, or the relationship between prose and metadata.  
   **Concrete fix:** Make answer text primary: for example, 16px body text at 1.5–1.6 line height, readable 13–14px metadata, and a consistent spacing scale. Put secondary actions in a keyboard-accessible menu; collapse completed tool details and thinking summaries while keeping pending approvals prominent.

10. **[med] “Matches mockup” points to an unavailable visual authority.**  
    **Reference:** §Layout heading; no explicit reference to `14-ui-system.md`.  
    **Why it matters:** `00` says the Stitch designs are absent and the prompt document is historical. Implementers could therefore import its violet message tint and older dimensions. Shared glass rules already exist in `14`; chat needs to specify their application to overlapping menus, tool cards, and message surfaces.  
    **Concrete fix:** Name `14` as the authority and add chat acceptance checks for composited text contrast, nested overlays, opaque fallback, and reduced-motion states. As an accent candidate, its existing soft green `#7FD6A4` gives **11.23:1** with `#0B0C0F` text; light `#E7E8EC` text on that fill gives only **1.42:1**. Reserve accent fills for selection/actions and keep body text on neutral glass surfaces.

11. **[med] Enter-to-send lacks autocomplete and composition exceptions.**  
    **Reference:** §Composer and §Rev 2: “Enter … only sends.”  
    **Why it matters:** Enter also commits IME text and selects `/` or `@` suggestions. Without explicit precedence, choosing a file or composing text can accidentally transmit an unfinished prompt.  
    **Concrete fix:** Suppress sending during IME composition. With a suggestion menu open, Enter selects the highlighted suggestion; a subsequent explicit send submits. Specify Escape behavior, focus return, accessible picker semantics, and a visible multiline-input label.

12. **[med] Streaming defines retained text but omits the interaction lifecycle.**  
    **Reference:** §Streaming: “with cancel. Partial output is kept on cancel.”  
    **Why it matters:** The spec leaves unclear whether Cancel affects only this run or invokes the global Stop behavior in `12`, which also pauses scheduling. It also omits scroll anchoring, screen-reader announcements, and handling late output during cancellation.  
    **Concrete fix:** Distinguish per-run Cancel from global Stop. Show cancelling/cancelled/failed states and retain the run link with partial output. Follow streaming only while the reader is at the bottom; otherwise offer “Jump to latest.” Announce meaningful status changes without announcing every token, and disable decorative motion under reduced-motion preferences.
